notes.summary: A–B hold: quantitative countable-tail estimates prove every modification-divisor order, and actual exp(-tu) ideals characterize the exact profile. Closed primary theorems apply in a common auxiliary Mκ background. BMP alone supplies no lower singularity volume.
notes.detailedSummary: Normalized hyperplane logarithms define a genuine strictly theta-psh potential. Uniform local L1 bounds for their pullbacks give tail-current mass and Lelong bounds proportional to the remaining coefficient sum on each fixed modification. Actual pulled-back multiplier-ideal orders recover normalized divisorial orders. The reverse implication uses the projective point theorem in a closed auxiliary background, with additional point blow-ups. BFJ’s right-limit ideals and exp(-2U) convention are converted using U=phi/2 and Guan–Zhou strong openness. BMP follows from bounded Bedford–Taylor Stokes with kappa.
notes.text:
A and B hold, with a necessary convention and background audit. This is a mathematical draft proof, not a conclusion drawn from finite experiments.

Write D=sum_j a_j[H_j], A_N=sum_{j<=N}a_j, delta_N=A-A_N, u_N=sum_{j<=N}a_j ell_j and R=theta-A kappa. Sections have unit coefficient norm, so ell_j<=0. In the prescribed convention, Poincare–Lelong gives dd^c ell_j=[H_j]-kappa. Unitary invariance reduces their FS mean to integral_0^1 2(1-x)log x dx=-3/2. Therefore u_N decreases, its L1 norm is 3A_N/2, and its limit u_0 is not identically minus infinity. All smooth positive volumes on compact X give equivalent L1 norms. The local decreasing-limit theorem, after a fixed smooth psh addition, gives the genuine canonical qpsh limit at every point. Distributionally, dd^c u_0=D-A kappa. The series D converges as a positive closed current, since its trace mass against kappa is A. Hence theta+dd^c u_0=R+D>=R>=c kappa for some c>0. Both u_0 and u=u_0-sup_X u_0 are genuine strictly theta-psh potentials. The supremum is finite. Theta is big in the genuine strict-current sense; indeed theta itself is positive.

Here is the countable passage on EVERY smooth compact modification pi:Z->P2, without assuming a closed positive metric on Z. Locally ell_s composed with pi is log|sum c_i F_i|^2 minus a fixed smooth function, where F_i represent pulled-back homogeneous coordinates. No nonzero constant linear combination is identically zero on a nonempty open set of Z: that set meets the bimeromorphic isomorphism locus, whose image contains an open set of P2. The unit coefficient sphere is compact. Convergent coefficients give locally uniformly convergent holomorphic combinations with a nonzero limit. Their logarithms converge in L1_loc. To check this, use local psh compactness: the logarithms are uniformly bounded above; a point where the limit is nonzero rules out convergence to minus infinity; pointwise convergence outside the limiting zero set identifies every L1 subsequential limit. A finite relatively compact chart cover gives a uniform bound integral_Z |ell_s composed with pi| dV_Z<=C_Z.

Consequently u_N composed with pi decreases pointwise and in L1 to the genuine u_0 composed with pi. For r_N=sum_{j>N}a_j ell_j, its pullback satisfies ||r_N composed with pi||_L1<=C_Z delta_N. Thus
T_N=delta_N pi^*kappa+dd^c(r_N composed with pi)=sum_{j>N}a_j[pi^*H_j]
is a positive CLOSED current. For any smooth Hermitian h_Z, distributional integration by parts gives
integral_Z T_N wedge h_Z=delta_N integral_Z pi^*kappa wedge h_Z+integral_Z(r_N composed with pi)dd^c h_Z<=C'_Z delta_N.
The smooth dd^c h_Z term is retained. The local Lelong monotonicity estimate bounds a positive closed current’s Lelong number at a ball center by its trace mass on that ball. A finite ball cover therefore gives nu(T_N,p)<=C''_Z delta_N, hence the same bound for generic divisor orders. Constants depend on the fixed modification; uniformity over all modifications is unnecessary.

For a fixed prime E, orders ord_E(pi^*H) are bounded as H varies. In the three-dimensional vector space of linear sections, sections vanishing to order at least m form a descending filtration with zero intersection, so some finite stage is zero. This proves convergence of b(E)=sum_j a_j ord_E(pi^*H_j). Finite additivity gives
nu_E(u_0 composed with pi)=sum_{j<=N}a_j ord_E(pi^*H_j)+nu_E(r_N composed with pi).
The final term lies between zero and C''_Z delta_N. Taking N to infinity proves nu_E(u composed with pi)=b(E) for EVERY E and pi. This is a quantitative tail argument, not an inference of Lelong continuity from weak convergence. All orders use nu_E(log|g|^2)=ord_E(g).

BMP holds in the original bounded-potential sense. Choose h=kappa. For every bounded genuine kappa-psh p, bounded Bedford–Taylor products give integral_X(kappa+dd^c p)^2=1. The cross term integrates to integral_X p dd^c kappa=0. The quadratic term is the global distribution dd^c(p dd^c p), whose integral is zero. Its recursive identity is justified locally after a smooth psh addition by bounded Bedford–Taylor approximation. Hence v_+(kappa)=1. No positive lower singularity volume is inferred from BMP.

For B, first reconstruct the following formula using ACTUAL pulled-back image ideals:
m_phi(E)=lim_{k->infinity}ord_E(I(k phi)O_Z)/k=nu_E(phi composed with pi). (1)
This holds for every genuine qpsh phi and every smooth compact modification. Locally set U=phi/2+rho, with rho smooth and sufficiently psh that U is psh. BFJ’s J(kU), defined using |g|^2 exp(-2kU), equals I(k phi). Its Bergman/Ohsawa–Takegoshi lower approximation bound makes the ideal potential less singular than kU, giving ord_E(I(k phi)O_Z)/k<=nu_E(phi composed with pi).
For the other bound, change variables in the integrability condition. If g belongs to I(k phi), then |g composed with pi|^2 exp(-k phi composed with pi)|Jac pi|^2 is integrable. Near a generic smooth point of E with equation s=0, closed-current divisorial subtraction gives phi composed with pi<=nu_E(phi composed with pi)log|s|^2+O(1). The Jacobian has order A_X(E)-1. Transverse integrability requires ord_E(g composed with pi)+A_X(E)>k nu_E(phi composed with pi). Therefore
nu_E(phi)-A_X(E)/k<=ord_E(I(k phi)O_Z)/k<=nu_E(phi).
Here A_X(E)=1+ord_E(Jac pi), also covering nonexceptional divisors. These estimates prove (1). They reconstruct BFJ Section 5.2, inequality (5.3), in the assignment’s conventions and apply directly to arbitrary pi. The point version follows from local Bergman approximation with maximal-ideal orders. It also proves that the generic order on the exceptional divisor of a point blow-up equals the normalized point Lelong number.

Choose a sufficiently large integer M with M kappa-theta>=0. Both u and any theta-psh v belong to the SAME CLOSED background PSH(P2,M kappa). Darvas–Xia, The closures of test configurations and algebraic singularity types, Section 2.4, Theorem 2.13, applies there: actual all-weight ideal equality is equivalent to point Lelong equality at every point of every projective smooth modification. Its hypotheses are compact Kahler X and a common smooth closed form representing a pseudo-effective class. They hold for M kappa, not for nonclosed theta.

If v has b(E) on every modification divisor, blow up any point y of any projective smooth modification Y. Apply the profile to this composite modification. The exceptional divisor recovers the normalized point order at y, so v and u have equal point Lelong numbers everywhere on all such Y. Theorem 2.13 gives I(tv)=I(tu) for every real t>0. Conversely, equality of these ideals at integer weights and (1) give equality of every generic divisor order on arbitrary smooth compact modifications. Thus the cited theorem’s projective scope has not silently been enlarged.

The primary local dependency is BFJ Theorem A, which originally uses right-limit J_+ ideals and exp(-2U). Guan–Zhou, A proof of Demailly’s strong openness conjecture, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 3.3, supply actual ideals and the exp(-phi) convention. Smooth local corrections do not change integrability. The retrieved DX version defines point Lelong numbers using log||z-y||; only its equality theorem, invariant under rescaling, is used. Formula (1) is independently reconstructed rather than copied from an unconverted numerical formula in Proposition 2.14.

Primary sources: https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0702487 ; https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v182-n2-p05-p.pdf ; https://research.chalmers.se/publication/528300/file/528300_Fulltext.pdf ; https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf . The exact application audit is sources/primary_source_audit.txt. Artifacts include n1.txt and evidence/check_algebra_output.json. Rerun: python check_algebra.py. Its exact FS integral and radial-threshold checks are algebraic evidence, not verification of the analytic proof.

notes.summary: C holds and is credited as known countable envelope equivalence: uniform residual upper bounds prove that q is genuine and canonically q~u, before any mass calculation. The same argument treats every smooth obstacle. It does not force every ideal-equivalent v to have ordinary type u.
notes.detailedSummary: Siu subtraction is applied only to a closed auxiliary current. Positivity after subtraction in the nonclosed background is proved separately by splitting measure coefficients on the countable divisor union and its complement. Canonical residual potentials and a closed-background sup-minus-mean estimate bound every competitor uniformly by u_0+C. The u competitor then sandwiches the envelope and preserves all pole values and every modification-divisor order. A maximum construction proves ordinary/ideal equality for u at every smooth obstacle.
notes.text:
C holds with IDEAL-EQUIVALENT competitors exactly as specified. No volume hypothesis is used to prove the ordinary type.

Use n1’s u_0, D and R. Let v have B’s exact profile, so v is ideal equivalent to u. For any competitor zeta<=0 with I(t zeta)=I(tu) at every weight, n1 gives nu_{H_j}(zeta)=a_j. Choose a fixed large M with beta=M kappa-theta>=0. S=M kappa+dd^c zeta is CLOSED and positive. Siu’s closed-positive-current decomposition gives S-D>=0, including the countable sum: subtract finitely many prescribed divisorial components, then take the decreasing positive-current limit. Coefficients are calibrated by dd^c log|s|^2=[s=0].

Positivity in the NONCLOSED background still needs proof. Let P=union_j H_j, a Borel pluripolar set with zero smooth-volume measure. Put T=theta+dd^c zeta=S-beta. On X\P the measure coefficients of S-D-beta equal those of positive T. On P, beta has zero measure coefficients and S-D is positive. Splitting each test pairing into these two parts proves T-D>=0 globally. This does not apply Siu’s theorem to T, and does not require the countable divisor union’s complement to be open.

The L1 difference zeta-u_0 has dd^c bounded below by -R. Its unique canonical qpsh representative psi_zeta satisfies R+dd^c psi_zeta=T-D>=0. The identity zeta=u_0+psi_zeta holds canonically everywhere: both sides are genuine qpsh functions representing the same L1 function, and canonical submean representatives are unique. In particular every pole of u_0 is a pole of zeta. No pointwise subtraction of infinities is performed.

Since R<=B kappa for some B, all residual potentials belong to the fixed CLOSED background PSH(X,B kappa). Guedj–Zeriahi’s sup-minus-mean estimate, Proposition 1.7 of Intrinsic capacities, applies on compact Kahler P2 with its scalar convention converted:
sup_X psi<=integral_X psi dV+C_B.
Because zeta<=0, integral_X psi_zeta dV<=-integral_X u_0 dV. Thus every competitor satisfies zeta<=u_0+C with ONE constant independent of the competitor.

Normalized u itself is a competitor. Therefore the pointwise supremum lies between u and u_0+C. Usc regularization preserves the upper bound since u_0+C is usc, and remains below zero. The envelope is genuine theta-psh: finite maxima preserve the fixed smooth lower bound -theta; their increasing Choquet envelope limit preserves positivity by L1 closure. For a nonclosed smooth bound, these stability statements follow locally by smooth convex maximum approximation and passage to the limit, while a large smooth psh addition supplies usual psh envelope stability. The lower bound by u excludes an identically minus infinity limit.

Consequently u<=q<=u_0+C canonically. This proves ordinary equivalence, including the same canonical pole set. Bounded differences preserve every multiplier ideal and every generic order on every modification, so q itself retains the countable profile. Profile preservation has been proved through the envelope rather than assumed from a general envelope theorem. An arbitrary starting v may have an additional unbounded residual with zero divisorial orders; we do not conclude v~u.

The argument works for EVERY smooth obstacle F. Choose c with u+c<=F. The mean bound now uses integral zeta<=integral F, yielding u+c<=q_F<=u_0+C_F. Thus q_F is genuine and ordinarily equivalent to u. For an ordinary competitor eta<=F with eta preceq u, max(eta,u+c) is below F, lies above eta, and is ordinarily equivalent to u. It is therefore an ideal-EQUIVALENT competitor. This proves P_(theta,F)[u]<=q_F. Conversely q_F<=F and q_F preceq u make q_F an ordinary competitor, proving equality. In particular P_theta[u]=q. This maximum argument preserves the distinction between the two competitor sets.

The assignment explicitly credits countable divisorial envelope equivalence as existing manuscript background. This independent reconstruction confirms and credits that result; no discovery or priority claim is made, and no sibling manuscript proof was inspected.

Primary dependencies: Siu, Invent. Math. 27 (1974), Section 2.1 and Theorems 2.2–2.3(A), pp. 80–82, for CLOSED positive currents, https://people.math.harvard.edu/~siu/siu_reprints/siu_analyticity_lelong_set_invent1974.pdf ; Guedj–Zeriahi Proposition 1.7, applied in B kappa, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0401302 . Finite subtraction and its countable limit are also explained in Demailly’s public textbook, Chapter III, pp. 180–181, https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf . notes.summary: D holds for every genuine w~q: bounded canonical residuals give corrected mass integral R²>0 throughout the entire ordinary type, so both extremal volumes coincide. Surface dimension and dd^c theta=0 are essential; no mass invariance for the whole ideal class is asserted.
notes.detailedSummary: Every ordinary representative has a bounded genuine R-psh residual, including at common poles. Closed auxiliary positive multilinearity gives a measure lower bound. Finite divisor removal gives mass upper bounds with vanishing tails, proving that the countable divisor part disappears from the auxiliary non-pluripolar square. Explicit smooth corrections recover the fixed nonclosed background. Bounded Bedford–Taylor integration and pluriclosedness then compute every mass in the defining infimum and supremum.
notes.text:
D holds for the ENTIRE ordinary type of q in the fixed nonclosed background. This is a mathematical draft argument.

Let w be ANY genuine theta-psh potential ordinarily equivalent to q. By n2, w~u_0 and its hyperplane orders are a_j. Apply n2’s closed auxiliary subtraction and separate nonclosed positivity argument, without any obstacle requirement. They give a genuine R-psh residual psi and the canonical identity w=u_0+psi, with R+dd^c psi>=0.

Ordinary equivalence implies |psi|<=C almost everywhere where w and u_0 are finite. These bounds hold everywhere for the canonical representative: after a local smooth psh addition, canonical values are limits of local averages of the L1 function, so both bounds pass to every point. Thus the residual is bounded globally, including at common poles. This covers all ordinary representatives, not a finite collection of logarithmic models.

To erase the countable divisor current carefully, choose M>A with beta=M kappa-theta>=0 and put
B=(M-A)kappa+dd^c psi,
S=M kappa+dd^c w=D+B,
D_N=sum_{j<=N}a_j[H_j],
S_N=S-D_N=B+(D-D_N).
These auxiliary currents are CLOSED and positive on compact Kahler P2; B has locally bounded potentials. BEGZ Proposition 1.6 gives finite non-pluripolar products, and Proposition 1.4 gives locality and positive multilinearity. Hence <S²>>=B² as measures.

For finite N, S=S_N outside the finite analytic union of H_j with j<=N. Both non-pluripolar measures ignore that union, so locality gives <S²>=<S_N²>. The class of S_N is (M-A+delta_N)[kappa]. Independently reconstruct its mass bound: write S_N=(M-A+delta_N)kappa+dd^c h_N, using canonical finite subtraction from w; normalize h_N<=0 and truncate by max(h_N,-k). Each bounded closed-background product has total mass (M-A+delta_N)² by Bedford–Taylor Stokes. Its restriction to {h_N>-k} defines the non-pluripolar measure in the limit. Therefore integral_X <S²><=(M-A+delta_N)². Let N tend to infinity. Since bounded B has integral B²=(M-A)², the positive measure <S²>-B² has total mass zero. Thus <S²>=B². No open complement of the whole countable union is assumed.

Also <S>=B. The degree-one non-pluripolar formula restricts S to the set where a local potential is finite. The pole set of w equals that of u_0; D is supported on its subset union_j H_j. B has bounded potentials and gives no mass to pluripolar sets. The restriction therefore removes D and retains all B. This uses BEGZ’s degree-one formula and the bounded Bedford–Taylor capacity property.

The prescribed corrected measure is consequently
MA_ext_theta(w)=<S²>-2 beta wedge <S>+beta²
=B²-2 beta wedge B+beta²
=(R+dd^c psi)².
The last expression is the bounded-potential Bedford–Taylor square with smooth corrections. It is finite and positive. Positivity can also be checked locally by convolving psi: smoothness of R gives R+dd^c psi_epsilon>=-o(1) times a fixed positive form. Add the vanishing error, then use bounded-potential Bedford–Taylor convergence. This does not require R to be closed.

Now retain the decisive surface differential hypothesis: dd^c R=dd^c theta-A dd^c kappa=0. Bounded-potential integration gives
integral_X R wedge dd^c psi=integral_X psi dd^c R=0,
and integral_X(dd^c psi)²=integral_X dd^c(psi dd^c psi)=0.
The recursive identity is justified locally after a smooth psh addition and gives a globally defined distribution. Hence
integral_X MA_ext_theta(w)=integral_X R²>0
for EVERY genuine theta-psh w~q. Since R>=c kappa, this number is at least c². Taking the infimum and supremum over the entire ordinary type proves
lower_volume_theta(q)=upper_volume_theta(q)=integral_X R².
This computes every mass in the defining set, rather than substituting one raw envelope mass for an extremal volume.

The statement does not cover every merely IDEAL-equivalent potential, whose residual may be unbounded. If dd^c theta is omitted, the calculation retains the extra term 2 integral_X psi dd^c theta. Higher dimensions require additional differential conditions. Neither extension is claimed. No closed mass-invariance theorem has been applied to theta or R.

Checked primary dependencies: Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 for bounded local potentials, https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf ; BEGZ Definition 1.1 and Propositions 1.4 and 1.6 for CLOSED positive currents on compact KAHLER P2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674 . The nonclosed correction and integration are derived above. Artifacts: n3.txt and sources/primary_source_audit.txt. Rerun finite algebra checks: python check_algebra.py. Execution success does not establish the analytic proof or its entire-type quantifier.

notes.summary: E–F hold: the cutoff construction gives a positive genuinely nonclosed pluriclosed projective background with infinite nonanalytic prime support and no hyperplane pencil. Both volumes are at least 1/16. Gauge transport preserves currents, measures, ideals and extrema, while transporting the obstacle.
notes.detailedSummary: The local tau differential is nonzero, while partial-barpartial tau vanishes globally even across the cutoff. Small epsilon is controlled by its kappa operator norm. Infinite positive hyperplane orders rule out any single analytic ideal type, and a Vandermonde identity excludes a pencil. The common mass is 9/16 minus an explicit positive torsion correction, with the pointwise residual bound proving positivity. Exact symbolic checks confirm the displayed algebra only. Gauge transport does not assert equality of newly normalized zero-obstacle envelopes.
notes.text:
E and F hold with the stated interpretation. The example is on a projective manifold with a genuinely NONCLOSED background. Failure of an analytic ideal TYPE means that no single analytic singularity type represents all its weighted ideals; individual multiplier ideals remain coherent.

Choose an affine coordinate ball and a real smooth compactly supported cutoff chi equal to one near its center. Extend alpha=chi |z_2|² dz_1 by zero and set tau=partial bar(alpha)+barpartial alpha. The summands are conjugates, so tau is real of type (1,1). Compact support makes its extension smooth. The identities partial²=barpartial²=0 and partial barpartial=-barpartial partial give partial barpartial tau=0 globally, including the cutoff region.

Where chi=1,
tau=bar z_2 dz_2 wedge dbar z_1-z_2 dz_1 wedge dbar z_2,
partial tau=dz_1 wedge dz_2 wedge dbar z_2,
barpartial tau=dz_2 wedge dbar z_1 wedge dbar z_2.
The last two forms have different types and are nonzero, including at the center. Thus d tau is nonzero. Let C_tau=sup_X ||tau||_op,kappa>0. Any positive epsilon with epsilon C_tau<=1/2 gives theta=kappa+epsilon tau>=kappa/2; for example epsilon=1/[4(1+C_tau)] works. This is pointwise positivity. Since kappa is closed, dd^c theta=0 but d theta=epsilon d tau is nonzero.

Set A=1/4, a_j=A2^(-j), t_j=2^(-j), j>=1. Their sum is A and their tail after N is A2^(-N). Normalize the defining vector (1,t_j,t_j²) by its Euclidean norm. The hyperplanes are pairwise distinct, and R=theta-A kappa>=kappa/4. Notes n1–n3 apply, giving both extremal volumes equal to integral_X R²>=1/16.

The differential correction can be displayed explicitly. Put eta=partial alpha. Since d(alpha+baralpha)=tau+eta+bareta, surface type considerations and Stokes give integral_X kappa wedge tau=0 and integral_X tau²=-2 integral_X eta wedge bareta. The measure eta wedge bareta is nonnegative in the complex orientation and is nonzero on an open subset near the center. Thus J=integral_X eta wedge bareta>0 and the actual common mass is
integral_X R²=9/16-2 epsilon² J.
Its positivity follows from R>=kappa/4. In particular one must retain this nonclosed correction rather than replace the answer by 9/16.

At the identity modification, n1’s countable-tail argument gives nu_{H_j}(u)=a_j>0 for infinitely many primes; n2 gives the same orders for q. A global analytic singularity type has only finitely many positive prime orders. Locally its divisorial singularities are components of the common zero set of finitely many holomorphic generators; compactness and a finite relatively compact chart cover give finitely many components globally. If an analytic type had all the same I(tu), n1’s actual ideal-order limit would force the same infinite positive prime support, a contradiction. This proves failure of an analytic ideal type as well as of an analytic ordinary type.

The lines do not form a single hyperplane pencil. A point common to all of them would give a degree-two polynomial Z_0+tZ_1+t²Z_2 with infinitely many roots, forcing all homogeneous coordinates to vanish. More precisely, their dual parameters [1:t:t²] lie on a nonsingular conic. A pencil is a projective line and meets this conic in at most two points. The determinant for three parameters a,b,t is (b-a)(t-a)(t-b), nonzero when they are distinct. Hence no three lines are concurrent and no infinite subfamily lies in one pencil. Pairwise intersections are [ab:-(a+b):1] and lie on no third H_j. No classification of arbitrary divisorial-fibration criteria is asserted.

The exact symbolic program returns partial barpartial tau=0; d tau has coefficient one on the two displayed 3-forms; and tau²=-2|z_2|² dz_1 wedge dz_2 wedge dbar z_1 wedge dbar z_2 where chi=1. It also verifies the Vandermonde and intersection polynomial identities, geometric tails, FS integral -3/2, and residual bound 1/16. These are exact algebra or finite checks. Infinite statements follow from the identities and mathematical proofs, not finite sampling.

For F, let f be smooth real, theta'=theta+dd^c f and w'=w-f. Then theta'+dd^c w'=theta+dd^c w as actual currents. Transport in both directions preserves genuine qpsh representatives, canonical poles and all finite ordinary inequalities, so it is a bijection between the specified ordinary types. At every weight, exp(-t w')=exp(tf)exp(-tw), with the smooth factor bounded above and below by positive constants. Thus I(tw')=I(tw).

Corrected measures are also identical. Choose a sufficiently large smooth closed auxiliary Omega, and transport it to Omega'=Omega+dd^c f. The positive closed auxiliary current Omega'+dd^c w' equals Omega+dd^c w, while Omega'-theta'=Omega-theta. Every term in the non-pluripolar smooth correction polynomial is therefore unchanged. On P2, Omega=M kappa can be chosen large enough for both smooth auxiliaries; the same argument is local with a large smooth strictly psh auxiliary in arbitrary dimension whenever the specified correction product is defined. The ordinary-type bijection and measure equality preserve both the infimum and the supremum of total masses.

Obstacles transport as well:
P_(theta',F-f)[v-f]_I=P_(theta,F)[v]_I-f.
Therefore q-f corresponds to obstacle -f. It need not be the newly normalized ZERO-obstacle envelope. Nonclosedness is preserved since d dd^c f=0. No modification mass law or zero-volume converse is asserted.

notes.summary: A scoped intrinsic sufficient criterion follows from actual birational ideal orders and a strictly positive pluriclosed residual. Known countable-envelope overlap is credited. Arbitrary nonclosed positivity and the remaining unrestricted zero-volume questions are untouched; candidate=false.
notes.detailedSummary: On P2, if actual pulled-back I(kv) orders divided by k equal a summable hyperplane profile on every modification divisor, and theta is positive pluriclosed with theta-Aκ>0, then the ideal-equivalent envelope has lower and upper singularity volumes equal to the residual square. The nonclosed example meets the criterion beyond finite analytic support and a single pencil. All four assertions for the constructed u follow directly, including stretching, but they are not asserted for every v in its ideal class. This answers only a sufficient family in original P06 part one, not a classification or any unrestricted zero-volume implication.
notes.text:
The reconstructed A–F give the following scoped intrinsic ideal/divisorial sufficient criterion. They do not solve the full exact original P06, so candidate remains false.

On P2 with standard kappa, retain fixed smooth positive theta with dd^c theta=0. For genuine theta-psh v define from ACTUAL pulled-back image ideals
m_v(E)=lim_{k->infinity}k^(-1)ord_E(I(kv)O_Z),
for E on pi:Z->X. Suppose distinct hyperplanes H_j and positive a_j satisfy A=sum_j a_j<infinity, theta-A kappa>0, and
m_v(E)=sum_j a_j ord_E(pi^*H_j)
for EVERY prime E on EVERY smooth compact modification. Note n1 proves existence of the limit and its normalized Lelong interpretation. The condition uses supplied ideal data and the explicit smooth residual, not an unknown envelope or its mass. It does not convert theta into a line-bundle curvature.

Then the specified IDEAL-EQUIVALENT envelope q=P_theta[v]_I satisfies
lower_volume_theta(q)=upper_volume_theta(q)=integral_X(theta-A kappa)²>0.
The proof is n1’s countable all-modification tail and exact ideal equivalence, n2’s canonical envelope type, and n3’s mass computation for EVERY ordinary representative. The genuinely nonclosed example in n4 has infinite positive prime support, no analytic ideal type and no hyperplane pencil; its common extremal volume is at least 1/16. Actual image ideals are used, without assuming that a potential restricts genuinely to a divisor.

For the explicit constructed u, all four original positive-volume assertions hold directly. Note n2 proves ordinary/ideal equality at zero and every smooth obstacle. Ordinary equivalence and n3 prove equality of upper singularity volumes. To verify the original STRETCHING definition, choose C with q<=u+C. For each real t>=1 set a_t=u-(t-1)C. It is genuine theta-psh and t^(-1)a_t+(1-t^(-1))q<=u. Interpret this canonically at common poles, with the t=1 endpoint a_1=u. Also u preceq q. Thus u belongs to E_env(X,theta,q), without replacing stretching by envelope equality. For an arbitrary v with the ideal profile, the result establishes positivity of its q; it does not assert v~q or all four conditions for v.

The overlap is explicit. Analytic-type equality and finite-divisor residual polynomials are known ingredients. The assignment credits countable divisorial ordinary/ideal envelope equivalence as existing manuscript background; n2 reconstructs and credits it rather than claiming discovery. The substantive verification extends the residual mass calculation to a summable countable profile, proves the tail on every modification, and retains the entire canonical ordinary-type quantifier in a genuinely nonclosed pluriclosed surface background.
